verdicts.explanation: The paper reports 0.19 mS/cm room-temperature conductivity for Li0.5Mg0.5Al0.5PO4 from Arrhenius fitting of CHGNet-MD data, and 0.38 eV for that configuration. Origin is correctly computational and the secondary fields are null as the paper gives no synthesis data.
The paper reports 0.024 mS/cm room-temperature conductivity and 0.52 eV for Li0.5TiPO4.5F0.5 from CHGNet-MD, so the value, temperature, and computational origin are all correct.
The 2.8 mS/cm value is the mean of three 200 ps fine-tuned CHGNet MD runs at 300 K for LATP, as stated in Section 2.4, so the material, temperature, and computational origin are correct.
The paper states the fine-tuned model predicts 8.6 mS/cm at 300 K for LATP and a migration barrier of 0.21 eV, both computed in this work.
The 5.1 mS/cm value is the AIMD reference computed in this paper for LATP at 300 K, with the 0.22 eV AIMD barrier, so computational origin and AIMD method are correct.
The paper states the pre-trained CHGNet model predicts 57 mS/cm at 300 K for LATP, which is a computed value from this work, and no activation energy is attributed to this value.

The roughly 1 mS/cm and 0.28 eV values for LATP are explicitly attributed to experimental literature (refs 30-32), not measured here, and the paper gives no measurement temperature, so null is correct.
